stated: Reform UK will lift the VAT threshold to £150,000 to free up small entrepreneurs from red tape.

source.quote: Lift the VAT Threshold to £150,000 Free up small entrepreneurs from red tape.

bearing_set.reason: Businesses currently VAT-registered between £85k–£150k turnover could reduce consumer-facing prices by removing the 20% VAT charge, directly affecting what households pay for goods and services from small traders.

Lifting the threshold reduces compliance costs and improves margins for small entrepreneurs and sole traders in the £85k–£150k band, materially affecting the viability and income of that cohort of working people.
Businesses with turnover between £90k–£150k would exit VAT registration, directly reducing their tax-compliance costs and potentially increasing net income for small business owners.

Removing VAT liability for an estimated bracket of currently-registered businesses reduces Exchequer VAT receipts; if unfunded, this materially widens the deficit — a concrete fiscal cost with a specific revenue-loss mechanism.

The VAT 'cliff edge' is a documented distortion that suppresses business growth; raising the threshold removes a drag on investment, hiring and firm scaling, plausibly improving productivity and business dynamism.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: a direct tax-burden reduction for affected small businesses (O11), a revenue cost to public finances if unfunded (O12), and a supply-side/dynamism gain from removing the cliff-edge distortion (O13). Consumer price effects (O2) are too contingent on pass-through decisions to clear the non-negligible bar at this stage.
